chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, from Abū Sārah, who said:

I asked Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about Mut'ah (temporary marriage), so he said to me: 'It is permissible, and do not marry except a chaste woman, for indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: [Those who guard their private parts], so do not place your private part where you do not feel secure regarding your dirham (dowry/money).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on temporary marriage and the condition of chastity for the wife?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms the permissibility of Mut'ah while emphasizing the critical importance of selecting a chaste (‘ififa) partner to preserve both spiritual integrity and financial security. He links the Quranic command to guard one's private parts (23:5) to a practical economic rationale: marrying an unchaste woman risks the loss of the dowry (mahr), illustrating the Shia scholarly view that Mut'ah is not merely a legal permission but a structured institution requiring moral and financial prudence.
